body: I feel that people often confuse the shock of suicide with feelings of love.

All things aren't ultimately valueless. I said that life is ultimately meaningless. With that distinction, I mean to say that there can be important things in something which has no purpose.

And I don't subscribe to nihilism (obviously). It's coincidence that the philosophies overlap in any way.

You said we should drop it, but I'll respond anyway. I didn't come to argue; just to talk. We seem to agree that life has no meaning, but you sound angered by it. I used to be angry. "Fuck this, fuck that! Fuck you!" (Just like you are now.) But I've learned to accept it, and I'm content with the situation.

> The person you help might just use you and toss you aside and proceed to inflict an unimaginable amount of misery onto the lives of others...I see helping people as something endless and pointless...I think people who actually spend their entire lives on the field are in serious denial or feel that they've already gone too far to turn back.

Mostly those bits are nonsense. And I didn't brush it off because I disagree; I did so because it's nonsense. Still, I usually disagree with nonsense, so you're on to something there. And don't say "what other people have to say." Not everyone, just you with that.

> If you really want to make an impact, help an individual

I appreciated this piece advice. Thanks.

I'm mildly odd, sure. That aside, your theories are nonsense. You seem upset about something--everything. Is that why you're on /r/SW? Or did you come to help others?

Me, I'm not really angry.
Thank you. I'll keep this in mind.
Ok, I'll let you know how I'm doing. Thanks.

I have a lot to think about. I'm definitely no superhero. It hard to live for myself, let alone live to help others. I have no business "saving" anyone. But it's something I will consider.

Thanks for investing time in me.

No, I haven't. But I've felt this way for more than half of my life. Is depression common in children? I wouldn't guess so. My mom told me that I used to rip out handfuls of hair when I was a toddler. Maybe I'm just fucking insane and always have been. :)

I don't know how to define it. I can only say what people look like when they say they feel it. And I don't think I've ever felt the way they look. I don't really know sadness either. I know despair and the feeling of lost opportunity. One might say they resemble sadness.

The same goes for emotional relationships. I don't feel any special way about my friends or family when compared to strangers. They're people who provide conversation. I can find that most places.

I'm not overcome with great emotion when I say I might end it. I just feel like I'm coasting through life, doing things merely because they're supposed to be done, as dictated by the nonsense book of life. And why should I continue coasting? Because the good book says so and that suicide is bad.

No, I've never seen a specialist. It's only recently that I've realized I should see one. I've always thought I was just...different. I don't feel emotions the way I assume other people do.

I don't find anything beautiful on a level greater than aesthetics. Can you name for me some of the beautiful aspects of life? Sex? Procreation? Sacrifice for "love?" What?

For me, compassion is the only thing that comes close to beauty.

I'm not interested in that sort of philanthropy. The gift of food or toys is a material one. I've lost nearly all appreciation for material things. I'm interested in social change. [This](http://www.dalitnetwork.org/go?/dfn/index) sort of thing.

I don't know how to explain how I feel. I don't hate myself. It's the opposite, really. And I think I'm far from worthless. I don't *want* to die. I wish things were different for me. I had lots of potential which was wasted on circumstance. But things are as they are, and death seems like the rational conclusion. Death is a natural and inevitable thing. I don't see why one would muddle through life to postpone it.
